reading.body:
Google NBY-2 is part of a multi-county data center campus in the New Albany and Columbus area that Google has committed $1.7 billion to develop across Franklin, Licking, and Fairfield counties. Google does not publish power capacity, square footage, or exact addresses for individual buildings within this campus, only aggregate state-level investment figures. This facility-level opacity is Google's stated disclosure policy and prevents direct measurement of this building's capacity.

Within Ohio's mapped data center infrastructure, which includes 76 facilities, only 8 operators have published power figures totaling 60.4 MW of disclosed capacity. NBY-2 does not appear among those 8 published specs, placing it outside Ohio's ranked set by disclosed megawatts. The New Albany corridor where NBY-2 sits has also attracted AWS and Meta as major hyperscale investors, indicating this region has become a preferred cluster for large operators, though individual facility capacities remain undisclosed.

Without published specifications, NBY-2's relevance to AI scaling cannot be measured against the binding grid constraints this site tracks. The investment scale and hyperscaler concentration suggest material significance to regional power demand and supply planning, but translating that into racks, accelerators, or grid load requires assumptions about typical utilization densities that would obscure rather than clarify the actual deployment.
